first.rationale: Two of the three current problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are funnel-mechanics problems, and the inherited record points at onboarding simplification as the lever that moves both (memory_86 on completion/time-to-value, memory_31 on first-week activation, with memory_91 as a downstream complement). Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the emotionally obvious answer to the competitor's entry pricing, but it addresses only the acquisition symptom, is the direction most likely to buy volume at the cost of margin and account quality, and the primary objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue rather than this quarter's logo count. So I am spending the scarce verification budget on the memories I intend to ACT on, not the one I intend to decline: memory_31 and memory_86 are load-bearing here, and if either is weak the whole plan should change. Specifically I want the archive to tell me (a) whether those lifts were measured on downstream qualified revenue/retention or only on the proximal funnel metric, (b) whether the effect persisted past the measurement window, and (c) for memory_31, which fields were cut — removing signup fields can lift activation while quietly degrading lead qualification, routing, and enterprise identification, which would trade a visible funnel win for an invisible revenue loss. That is the concrete downstream-value risk I am flagging. Note also a tension in the inherited record: memory_44 says enterprise converts better via sales-assisted paths, so any signup simplification must not strip the signals that route enterprise prospects to demo-request. I am therefore running this as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout: instrument qualified-revenue and lead-quality metrics alongside completion/activation, hold enterprise routing fields, and only scale if the downstream metrics stay clean. The inherited summaries are compressed conclusions, not evidence; I am treating them as a strong prior to test, not a settled fact to deploy on.
